beats.intro: Learning module ten. [[sub]]Pricing an option with a one-period binomial model.
beats.model: [[why]]A forward can be replicated without knowing where the price will go. An option cannot: its payoff is one-sided, so we need a model of the future price. [[tree]]The simplest is the binomial model. Over one period, the price either goes up to S one u, [[up]]which is R u times S zero, [[down]]or down to S one d, which is R d times S zero. [[q]]Call the probability of an up move q. Surprisingly, we will not need it. [[vol]]What matters is the spread between the up and down prices: that spread is the volatility.
beats.tree: [[ex]]An example. A one-year European call with an exercise price of one hundred euros. The underlying is at eighty. [[up]]It can rise to one hundred ten, a gross return of one point three seven five. [[down]]Or fall to sixty, a gross return of point seven five. [[cu]]If it rises, the call pays one hundred ten minus one hundred: ten euros. [[cd]]If it falls, the call expires worthless. [[unk]]The only unknown is the call's value today.
beats.hedge: [[idea]]The trick: build a portfolio with no risk. Sell one call, and buy h units of the underlying. [[vu]]If the price goes up, the portfolio is worth one hundred ten h, minus ten. [[vd]]If it goes down, it is worth sixty h. [[eq]]Choose h so the two are equal. [[h]]The hedge ratio is the change in the option, ten, divided by the change in the underlying, fifty: point two. [[check]]With h equal to point two, the portfolio is worth twelve euros either way. Twenty-two minus ten, or twelve.
beats.price: [[rf]]A portfolio with a certain payoff must earn the risk-free rate, five percent. [[v0]]So today it is worth twelve divided by one point oh five: eleven euros forty-three. [[c0]]The portfolio is point two units of the underlying, worth sixteen euros, minus the call. So the call is worth sixteen minus eleven forty-three: four euros fifty-seven. [[arb]]At any other price, someone could build a synthetic risk-free asset earning more than the risk-free rate.
beats.rn: [[eq]]There is a shortcut. Define the risk-neutral probability, pi: one plus r, minus R d, divided by R u minus R d. [[pi]]Here, one point oh five minus point seven five, over one point three seven five minus point seven five: point four eight. [[val]]The option's value is its expected payoff using pi, discounted at the risk-free rate. Point four eight times ten, plus point five two times zero, is four eighty. Divided by one point oh five: four fifty-seven again. [[q]]Notice what is missing: the real-world probability q, and investors' attitude to risk. Only volatility and the risk-free rate matter. This is risk-neutral pricing.
beats.hightest: [[setup]]Hightest considers selling a one-year call on a fifty dollar stock, with an exercise price of fifty-five. The stock can rise or fall twenty percent. The rate is five percent. [[pi]]The risk-neutral probability is one point oh five minus point eight, over point four: point six two five. [[call]]The call pays five dollars in the up state, so it is worth point six two five times five, discounted: two dollars ninety-eight. [[put]]A put with the same terms pays fifteen in the down state: point three seven five times fifteen, discounted, is five thirty-six. [[parity]]Check put-call parity: fifty plus five thirty-six equals two ninety-eight plus fifty-five discounted. Both sides are fifty-five thirty-six. [[vol]]If the stock could move forty percent instead, the call rises to eight oh four, and the put to ten forty-two. More volatility, more option value. [[view]]And Hightest's own view on the stock does not change the price at all.
beats.wrap: [[w1]]The binomial model lets the price move up by R u or down by R d; the spread is the volatility. [[w2]]A hedge ratio of the option change over the price change makes a risk-free portfolio. [[w3]]That portfolio earns the risk-free rate, which pins down the option price. [[w4]]Equivalently, value equals the risk-neutral expected payoff, discounted at the risk-free rate.
beats.finish: That's the end of learning module ten, and of the derivatives volume.
